name: The weak verb
definition: A verb with a weak letter (wāw, yāʾ or alif) among its root letters. These letters often change or drop when it is conjugated.
body: قَالَ (he said) has the root ق و ل: its wāw shows in يَقُولُ but becomes an alif in قَالَ. رَمَى (he threw) has the root ر م ي. وَعَدَ (he promised) loses its wāw in يَعِدُ.

The books name the weak verb by the place of the weak letter: mithāl at the start (وَعَدَ), ajwaf in the middle (قَالَ), nāqiṣ at the end (رَمَى). The rules for these changes, iʿlāl, are a large part of ṣarf.
